properties.natural_language: Before beginning a transaction via EDGE-BEGIN-TX, the system must be in a clean state with no active snapshots to ensure snapshot stack consistency

The snapshot stack depth must be non-negative at all times: every commit or rollback must correspond to a prior begin-transaction, and the system must never attempt to commit or rollback without an active snapshot
After a rollback via EDGE-ROLLBACK-RESULT, all state modifications made since the corresponding begin-transaction must be fully reverted, with the trie restored to its snapshot point

Nested transaction snapshots must follow strict LIFO ordering: a nested begin-transaction from STATE-ACTIVE-SNAPSHOT creates a new snapshot layer, and the innermost snapshot must be committed or rolled back before outer ones
Before querying a nonexistent account via EDGE-GET-NONEXISTENT, the get_account action must return EMPTY_ACCOUNT as the default value, never null or an error
After setting an account via EDGE-SET-RESULT, the account must be retrievable from the state trie with correct nonce, balance, code, and storage root values
The modify_state function must always auto-destroy accounts that become empty (zero nonce, empty code, zero balance) after modification, enforcing EIP-161 state clearing
After destroying an account via EDGE-DESTROY-RESULT, the account address must return EMPTY_ACCOUNT on subsequent queries and all associated storage must be removed
Account creation tracking via EDGE-MARK-CREATED must correctly record accounts created in the current transaction for EIP-6780 SELFDESTRUCT rules enforcement
Before incrementing a nonce via EDGE-INCREMENT, the account must exist in the state trie with a valid current nonce value
After setting account code via EDGE-SET-CODE, the code hash in the account must match the keccak256 of the deployed bytecode
Before writing to storage via EDGE-SET-REQUIRES-ACCOUNT, the account must be verified to exist; storage writes to nonexistent accounts must be rejected
Setting a storage slot to U256(0) must always delete the slot from the trie via EDGE-SET-ZERO, and reading an empty slot must always return U256(0)
Before reading original storage via EDGE-GET-ORIGINAL, a pre-transaction snapshot must exist to provide the initial value for gas refund calculations
After destroying all storage via EDGE-DESTROY-RESULT, every storage slot for the address must be removed and subsequent reads must return U256(0)
Transient storage values must only persist within a single transaction: after EDGE-TX-END-CLEAR, all transient storage must be completely cleared regardless of transaction outcome
After TSTORE via EDGE-TSTORE-RESULT, the value must be immediately readable via TLOAD for the same address and slot within the same transaction
Before processing an eth_config RPC request via EDGE-RPC-CALL, the external RPC client must provide a valid JSON-RPC formatted request targeting the eth_config method
Rate limiting must be enforced for all eth_config requests: requests exceeding the recommended 1-second interval must transition to STATE-RATE-LIMIT-EXCEEDED and not proceed to response building
After building a configuration response via EDGE-BUILT, the response must contain current, next (or null), and last (or null) fork configurations reflecting the most recent block header state
Before building the response, the node must be in STATE-NODE-RUNNING with loaded fork configurations; requests to uninitialized nodes must fail validation
Configuration caches must be invalidated on every fork transition: after EDGE-PURGE, cached configuration data must be cleared and fresh data required for subsequent queries
After crossing a fork boundary via EDGE-POST-FORK, the current configuration must reflect the new fork rules, the previous fork becomes 'last', and any previously scheduled fork becomes current
The configuration loading sequence must always follow the order: read current, then next, then last. Each step must complete before the next begins
After configuration comparison via EDGE-MATCH, if all fields match between own and reference configurations, the validator is confirmed ready for the upcoming fork
After detecting configuration mismatch via EDGE-DIFFER, an alert must be sent to the operator via EDGE-ALERT so corrective action can be taken before fork activation
Before querying reference node configuration via EDGE-QUERY-REF, the validator must have successfully retrieved their own node configuration first
Before an attacker can query configuration via EDGE-EXPOSED, the node's RPC endpoint must be externally accessible; restricting access via EDGE-RESTRICT prevents this attack vector entirely
Rate limiting must prevent DDoS attacks: applying rate limits via EDGE-RATE-LIMIT must transition the system to STATE-DDOS-MITIGATED, blocking resource exhaustion
After cross-checking configuration from a potentially dishonest node via EDGE-CROSS-CHECK, any mismatch must result in STATE-DISHONESTY-DETECTED to alert the operator
After an attacker queries configuration via EDGE-QUERY-CONFIG, the leaked configuration data must not contain any secret keys, authentication tokens, or private network topology details
Before configuring the light client via EDGE-UNCONFIG-TO-CONFIG, the operator must provide a trusted block root from within the weak subjectivity period and valid genesis data

The light client synchronization lifecycle must follow strict ordering: unconfigured -> configured -> clock init -> bootstrap -> store init -> committee updates -> real-time tracking. No state may be skipped
After applying a forced update via EDGE-FORCE-TO-SYNCED, the light client must resume normal real-time tracking in STATE-LC-SYNCED with an advanced finalized header
Before verifying bootstrap data via EDGE-ROOT-TO-VERIFY-BOOTSTRAP, a trusted block root must be established that corresponds to a genuinely finalized block on the canonical chain

All LightClientUpdate messages must be verified against the known sync committee via EDGE-COMMITTEE-TO-VERIFY-UPDATE before the new committee is accepted; unverified updates must never advance the light client state
After verifying a finality update via EDGE-VERIFY-FINALITY-TO-HEADER, the finalized header must be updated only if the sync committee aggregate signature is valid and attests to the finalized block

The stall detection mechanism must continuously monitor finality update reception: if no finality updates are received for an entire sync committee period, the system must transition through EDGE-DETECT-TO-STALLED and attempt forced recovery

Before executing any alt_bn128 precompile via EDGE-IDENTIFY, the calling contract must have sufficient gas remaining after the fork to cover the reduced costs (150 for ECADD, 6000 for ECMUL, 34000k+45000 for pairing)
Gas costs must be deterministic: ECADD must always cost exactly 150 gas, ECMUL exactly 6000 gas, and pairing exactly 34000*k + 45000 gas regardless of input values post-Istanbul fork
After gas deduction via EDGE-GAS-OK, the remaining gas must be exactly the pre-call gas minus the computed precompile cost, and execution must proceed to STATE-GAS-DEDUCTED
Precompile selection must be deterministic based on target address: 0x06 must always select ECADD, 0x07 ECMUL, 0x08 pairing with no other addresses accepted
All precompile executions must produce deterministic results: given the same input data, ECADD, ECMUL, and pairing operations must return identical results across all client implementations
After computation completes via EDGE-RETURN, the result must be returned to the calling context and EVM execution must resume at the next instruction in STATE-CALL-RETURNED
Before proceeding to curve validation via EDGE-CHECK-CURVE, input length must be validated first; only inputs passing length validation may proceed to point-on-curve checks
All input points must be validated to lie on the alt_bn128 curve before computation: points failing EDGE-POINT-BAD validation must cause the precompile to fail, never produce incorrect results
Before publishing a blob sidecar via EDGE-CREATED-TO-SUBNET, the proposer must have created a valid BlobSidecar with correct KZG commitment, proof, signed header, and Merkle inclusion proof

Blob sidecar validation must enforce all checks: index < MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK, correct subnet mapping, valid proposer signature, valid inclusion proof, and valid KZG proof. Failure of any check must result in rejection
Blob requests must respect the retention window: requests for blobs outside MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS (~18 days) must return ResourceUnavailable error code 3 via EDGE-CHECK-UNAVAILABLE
Before accepting a beacon block via gossip, the blob KZG commitment count must be validated via EDGE-RECV-TO-BLOB-COUNT to ensure it does not exceed MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK
The attestation propagation window per EIP-7045 must accept attestations from the current or previous epoch only; this extended window must be consistently enforced

The STATIC flag must be correctly propagated: STATICCALL always sets STATIC=true for the child context, CALL inherits the parent's STATIC flag, and the flag is always restored to its pre-call value upon return
When STATIC=true, all state-modifying opcodes (CREATE, CREATE2, LOG*, SSTORE, SELFDESTRUCT, CALL with value) must be prohibited and throw an exception via EDGE-THROW-ON-PROHIBITED
Before calling an untrusted external contract via EDGE-EXT-CONTRACT-RECEIVED, the caller should use STATICCALL to guarantee no state modifications can occur in the called context

After a malicious external code attempts state modification in static context via EDGE-ATTEMPT-MODIFY, the modification must be blocked via EDGE-MODIFICATION-REJECTED and the state must remain unchanged
Before executing upgrade_to_bellatrix via EDGE-CHECK-TO-UPGRADE, the fork epoch condition must be met: slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0 and computed epoch == BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH (144896)
After upgrade completion via EDGE-UPGRADE-DONE, the beacon state must have Bellatrix format with updated fork version (0x02000000), empty ExecutionPayloadHeader, and all Altair fields preserved

During fork upgrade, all existing Altair state fields must be copied unchanged via EDGE-INIT-TO-COPY: validators, balances, slashings, participation, sync committees must be bit-identical before and after upgrade
After fork object update via EDGE-UPDATE-TO-INIT, previous_version must be set to the Altair fork version, current_version to BELLATRIX_FORK_VERSION, and epoch to BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH
When multiple forks activate at the same epoch, upgrades must execute sequentially in chronological order via EDGE-MULTI-TO-SEQ; no upgrade may be skipped or reordered
Before dropping pre-merge history via EDGE-DROP-HISTORY, all deposit logs must be processed by the consensus layer (STATE-DEPOSIT-LOGS-PROCESSED) and eth/69 protocol must be implemented
After history expiry via EDGE-HISTORY-DROPPED, the sync algorithm must be adjusted to start from the merge block, not genesis, via EDGE-ADJUST-SYNC
Before serving pre-merge data requests via EDGE-RPC-REQUEST, the node must check local storage first via EDGE-CHECK-LOCAL; only if data is not local should alternate sources be queried
All data retrieved from external sources (e2store, Portal Network, EIP-7801) must be validated via EDGE-VALIDATE-DATA before being served to clients; unvalidated external data must never be returned
History expiry activation must follow strict ordering: devnet testing -> Sepolia activation -> Pectra fork -> mainnet activation. No stage may be skipped
Before executing a sub-call via EDGE-EXECUTE-SUBCALL, gas must be charged for input memory expansion only; output memory gas must not be charged until the sub-call returns

After sub-call return via EDGE-SUBCALL-RETURN, output memory gas must be charged for output_start + min(output_size, n) where n is actual return data size; insufficient gas leads to STATE-GAS-DEPLETED-END
Memory expansion must follow the sequence: expand for input first, then expand for output after return. MSIZE must always reflect the actual expanded memory size at each step
Output bounds must be enforced: sub-call return data must be constrained to [output_start, output_start + output_size) to prevent arbitrary memory writes by called contracts
Before processing a type-4 transaction via EDGE-RPC-SUBMIT, the transaction must have a non-empty authorization list and a non-null destination address
The sender nonce must be incremented before authorization processing: EDGE-INC-NONCE must occur between sender validation and authorization tuple processing
After authorization processing and execution via EDGE-EXECUTED, the transaction must complete with a definitive success or revert status, and all applied delegations must persist

Authorization tuple validation must follow strict ordering: chain ID check -> nonce bound check -> authority recovery -> s-value check -> accessed address marking -> code state check -> nonce match. Failed validations at any step must skip the authorization, not revert the transaction
Before recovering authority via EDGE-RECOVER, the chain ID must be validated and nonce must be within bounds (< 2^64 - 1); only then may ecrecover with MAGIC prefix be applied
After writing a delegation indicator via EDGE-DELEGATION-WRITTEN, the authority's code must be exactly 0xef0100 concatenated with the 20-byte target address (23 bytes total)
After clearing delegation via EDGE-DELEGATION-CLEARED, the authority's code must be set to the empty hash, and the authority nonce must be incremented by 1
Gas refunds must be applied correctly: non-empty authority accounts must receive (PER_EMPTY_ACCOUNT_COST - PER_AUTH_BASE_COST) refund via EDGE-APPLY-REFUND before delegation is written

Delegation resolution must be single-level: when detecting a delegation indicator, only the first level target's code is loaded. If the target also has a delegation indicator, it must not be recursively resolved
Delegation targets that are precompile addresses must be treated as empty code via EDGE-EXEC-EMPTY; precompile code must never be executed in a delegated EOA context
After delegated code execution via EDGE-DELEGATED-EXEC-DONE, the code must have executed in the EOA's context (using EOA's address, storage, and balance), not in the target contract's context
Intrinsic gas calculation must include PER_EMPTY_ACCOUNT_COST (25000) per authorization tuple in addition to standard base gas and access list costs
Delegation access costs must correctly apply COLD_ACCOUNT_READ_COST (2600) for first access and WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST (100) for subsequent accesses to the same delegation target

Before an attacker can replay an authorization via EDGE-ATTACKER-REPLAY, the system must verify that the authorization nonce matches the current account nonce; replayed authorizations with stale nonces must be blocked

The tx.origin == msg.sender invariant is broken by EIP-7702: delegated EOA code can make calls where msg.sender equals tx.origin in non-topmost frames. Contracts must not rely on this check for security
Storage collision between EOA state and delegation target must be mitigated via ERC-7201 namespaced storage; delegate contracts should use EDGE-USE-NAMESPACE to ensure isolation
